title: Radio bands: Les Hite, Fletcher Henderson, Carroll Dickerson, Ellington
summary: Moore lists the bands he heard on radio and in Chicago that oriented him toward jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: since -- as far as they ever were, they were at Armstrong. Now, there were -- over the radio at Sherman I used to hear bands like Les Hite and then there was a band called the Irving Brothers. And they were coming to the network from Culver City. Les Hite was there, Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club. And a . . .
What about the Earl Hines' Orchestra?
The Earl Hines? They were in Chicago. I didn't hear too much of Earl Hines -- at that time.

No, but while I was -- I'm going back to Chicano. While I was in Blue Island, I used to hear broadcasts of Fletcher Henderson. And a -- that's another fellow that a, that really, really started me into thinking of jazz also. While I was Chicago, in Chicago -- I'm going back again -- I used to hear Carroll Dickerson, and he was at the Vendome. Then there was Tiny, Tiny Parham, I think that's the name, I'm not sure, Tiny. It also -- as I say, Jean Goldkette and Cotton Pickers. . . And one time, . . .
Yes, yes, yes. One time I was walking the streets, and I picked up a circular, and it said, 'now appearing at' such-and-such a place, I forgot where they were appearing,
"Duke Ellington and his Washingtonians". And there was Sonny Greer and . . .
Right, right, right. They also only -- they have only seven men; I remember that time. So, that's how I got oriented into jazz. I just a, love jazz all through that.
